name: Rock snail
summary: Ốc đá, also called ốc suối or ốc núi, is a small snail from rock crevices and forest caves, chewy, fragrant, and very sweet. It is boiled, steamed with ginger or lemongrass, or stir-fried, and dipped in chẩm chéo.
origin: Bản Đôn and Phố Đoàn, Pù Luông. Sources: The Thanh Hoa Department of Culture, Sports and Tourism, 18 Mar 2022 and 16 May 2022; the Vietnam Airlines travel guide; VnExpress, 3 Jul 2023.
texture: Small, chewy, fragrant, and very sweet.
howToEat: Boiled, steamed with ginger or with lemongrass, made into a salad, stir-fried, or fried with lime leaf. Dip it in chẩm chéo rather than sweet-sour fish sauce.
The Vietnam Airlines guide calls it a rainy-season snail. The Bản Đôn list gives no season.
where: Bản Đôn, and Phố Đoàn on market day.
